  "text": "At the hardware shop, Martin placed the kitchen drawer on the counter.

“It won’t close,” he said.

The assistant lifted it and examined the runners. A teaspoon slid into one corner.

“Sorry.” Martin put the spoon in his pocket.

“Nothing wrong with these. Have you checked the cabinet?”

He had checked it on Sunday, kneeling on the floor while the kettle boiled. His father had fitted the kitchen twenty-six years earlier. There were pencil measurements inside every cupboard, some crossed out, some underlined twice.

“It catches halfway.”

The assistant pressed a thumb against the drawer’s back panel.

“Bit swollen. Been a leak?”

“Under the sink. That’s fixed now.”

Outside, someone was loading fence posts into a van. Each post struck the others with a hollow knock.

“You could sand this edge. Not much.”

The assistant showed him where, then fetched a sheet of sandpaper from a rack.

Martin had his father’s electric sander in the garage. He had tried it once. The dust bag had come loose, covering his shoes and the lower shelves in fine yellow powder.

“Will this do it?”

“Take your time. Keep trying the drawer.”

He paid for two sheets.

At home, he laid newspaper on the kitchen table. The drawer had left a clean rectangle inside the cabinet. At the back, beyond the runners, he could see a small red shape.

He reached in and brought out a plastic measuring spoon.

His father had looked for it one Christmas, opening cupboards while the gravy thickened.

Martin washed it, dried it, and put it beside the kettle. Then he began sanding."
